bib.title: mT5: A Massively Multilingual Pre-trained Text-to-Text Transformer

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; per-language tables 7-14 skimmed (only cited cells used).

question: Can the T5 text-to-text recipe be applied unchanged-as-possible to 101 languages with a new multilingual Common Crawl corpus, and how well does it do on multilingual benchmarks?
hypothesis: Scaling up a simple T5-style pre-training recipe on multilingual data is a viable alternative to more complex techniques (LM filtering, parallel data, intermediate tasks).
contributions: mT5, a multilingual T5 (300M to 13B) pre-trained on 101 languages
mC4, a multilingual variant of C4 from Common Crawl
Characterisation of 'accidental translation' in zero-shot generation and a simple fix (mixing in the pre-training task during fine-tuning)

method.summary: mT5 follows the T5.1.1 encoder-decoder recipe with a 250,000-wordpiece vocabulary, pre-trained with span corruption on mC4 (101 languages, sampled with exponent alpha=0.3) for 1M steps. It is fine-tuned on XTREME tasks cast as text-to-text in zero-shot, translate-train and in-language multitask settings.
method.task: multilingual span-corruption pre-training; XTREME fine-tuning (NLI, paraphrase, NER, extractive QA)

datasets.name: mC4
datasets.size: 6.6B pages, 6.3T tokens (107 cld3 languages, 101 counted); all 71 monthly Common Crawl scrapes
datasets.source: Public Common Crawl; language ID with cld3
datasets.preprocessing: Keep pages with >=3 lines of 200+ characters (line length filter); dedupe lines across documents; remove pages with bad words; drop pages with cld3 language confidence below 70%; keep languages with >=10,000 pages

datasets.name: XNLI
datasets.split: standard XTREME validation sets for early stopping

datasets.name: WikiAnn NER
datasets.preprocessing: Entities concatenated in order of appearance; target 'None' if no entities

datasets.name: SQuAD
datasets.preprocessing: Used for T5 vs mT5 comparison

datasets.name: Wikipedia (TFDS 2020)
datasets.source: TensorFlow Datasets, 103 languages, same languages as mBERT

models.name: mT5-Small
models.tokenizer: SentencePiece, character coverage 0.99999, byte-fallback, trained with pre-training language sampling rates

other.note: d_model and d_ff both scaled in larger models (T5.1.1: scales d_model as well as d_ff)
SQuAD numbers reproduced from Raffel et al. 2020

models.name: mBERT, XLM, XLM-R, InfoXLM, X-STILTs, VECO, RemBERT, FILTER

training.objective: T5 span corruption: 15% of tokens masked, average noise span length 3; fine-tuning teacher-forced maximum likelihood
training.batch_size: pre-training 1024 sequences; fine-tuning 2^17 tokens for most tasks, 2^16 for WikiAnn NER zero-shot, 2^20 for XNLI
training.steps: 1 million pre-training steps; fine-tuning steps not stated (checkpoint every 200 steps)
training.epochs: Fraction of an epoch for high-resource languages (English 2%)
training.seeds: TyDi QA zero-shot: median of five fine-tuning runs; others not stated

other.language_sampling: p(L) proportional to |L|^alpha, alpha=0.3 (alpha 0.2 and 0.7 ablated)
other.early_stopping: checkpoint every 200 steps, best on XTREME validation sets
other.domain_preserving_training: mix mC4 span-corruption task into XQuAD fine-tuning at 1:100 ratio, sentinel tokens removed from targets, alpha reduced 0.3 to 0.1
other.batch_size_note: Fine-tuning batch sizes printed as 217, 216, 220 tokens; read as 2^17, 2^16, 2^20 (superscripts lost in extraction)

inference.samples: TyDi QA zero-shot: median across five fine-tuning runs
inference.prompting: Tasks cast as text-to-text, label text or answer generated

metrics.name: Illegal prediction rate
metrics.definition: Prediction not a substring of the input context (XQuAD zero-shot); also after Unicode NFKC normalisation

eval.protocol: Three settings: zero-shot (English only), translate-train (English plus machine translations, using Hu et al. 2020 data), in-language multitask. Checkpoint chosen on XTREME validation sets.

limits: Illegal (non-substring) predictions remain a problem for generative models in zero-shot span selection; the DPT fix is shown only for XQuAD.
Ablations are on mT5-Large and XNLI zero-shot (XQuAD in appendix), single runs.
Hardware, compute time, optimiser and layer counts are not stated.
XLM-R sees over 6 times more tokens (6.3T) than mT5 (1T), so pre-training budgets differ.
mT5 benefits for translate-train comparisons depend on using English data in addition, differing from XTREME's setup.
